reason: Conversation 1 followed the expected sensible path: confirmed other kitchen sockets work, identified that an integrated machine is usually fed by a switched fused spur, explained plainly what a spur looks like when the homeowner asked, kept safety boundaries (no covers, no pulling the unit out, don't remove the fuse), and resolved the 'washer' isolator being off with no part recommended and engineer escalation only as a fallback. Conversation 2 refused to engage at all and pushed straight to an engineer, which for a renter would have meant a needless landlord callout for a problem fixed by flipping a switch. Minor quibble on Conversation 1 for speculating about mains filter/control board before the spur was checked, but it kept those as 'later' possibilities and never acted on them.
